J.'''" '''Wilcox''' (born December 30, 1990) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. The {{height|ft=6|in=5}} [[shooting guard]] played high school basketball at [[Pleasant Grove High School (Utah)|Pleasant Grove High School]] before going on to complete four years at the [[University of Washington]]. He was selected by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] with the 28th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]]. ==Early life== Wilcox was raised by his grandmother in [[Eastman, Georgia]], while his father, Craig, was away attending [[Brigham Young University|BYU]]. In 1995, at the age of four, Wilcox moved from [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] to [[Utah]] to live with his father.{{cite web|first=Scott|last=Johnson|url=http://www.heraldnet.com/article/20121213/SPORTS/712139915|title=Father a big influence on Huskies Wilcox|work=HeraldNet.com|date=December 13, 2012|accessdate=December 8, 2014}} As a youth, Wilcox played [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) basketball in the state of Utah. As early as the seventh grade, Wilcox starred alongside [[Tyler Haws]] on an AAU team called the Wildcats. Both Wilcox and Haws went on to play together on the Salt Lake City Metro.{{cite web|first=Todd|last=Dybas|url=http://blog.thenewstribune.com/uwsports/2013/03/19/wilcox-with-another-shot-in-front-of-the-home-folks/|title=Wilcox with another shot in front of the home folks|work=TheNewsTribune.com|date=March 19, 2013|accessdate=December 8, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141111041352/http://blog.thenewstribune.com/uwsports/2013/03/19/wilcox-with-another-shot-in-front-of-the-home-folks/|archive-date=November 11, 2014|url-status=dead}} ==High school career== Wilcox attended [[Pleasant Grove High School (Utah)|Pleasant Grove High School]] in [[Pleasant Grove, Utah]] where he starred alongside his cousin, LeSean, who went on to play for [[Salt Lake Community College]] from 2009 to 2011.{{cite web|url=http://www.slccbruins.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=19|title=LeSean Wilcox - 2009-10 Men's Basketball|work=slccbruins.com|accessdate=October 4, 2014}} As a freshman in 2005–06, he averaged 15.2 points per game, while as a sophomore in 2006–07, he averaged 23.7 points per game.{{cite web|url=https://sports.deseret.com/high-school/boys-basketball/athlete/CJ-Wilcox-boys-basketball/52760|title=High School Sports – C.J. Wilcox|work=DeseretNews.com|access-date=December 8, 2014}} As a junior in 2007–08, Wilcox averaged 23.7 points, six rebounds, 2.2 steals and two blocks per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=208057024|title=#23 C.J. Wilcox|work=GoHuskies.com|accessdate=July 10, 2014}} Wilcox was recruited by Utah, BYU, Utah State, San Diego University, Miami (FL), Florida State, Iowa State, Cal-Berkeley and others. In November 2008, he signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Washington]].{{cite web|url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/705262939/Vikings-guard-signs-with-Washington.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140729005219/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/705262939/Vikings-guard-signs-with-Washington.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 29, 2014|title=Vikings guard signs with Washington|work=DeseretNews.com|date=November 14, 2008|accessdate=July 10, 2014}} As a senior in 2008–09, Wilcox averaged 22.2 points per game as he was named to the Region 4 first team. Considered a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Wilcox was listed as the No. 24 shooting guard and the No. 108 player in the nation in 2009.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-C.J.-Wilcox-74730|title=C. J. Wilcox Recruiting Profile|work=Rivals.com|accessdate=November 5, 2015}} On February 12, 2016, Wilcox had his #23 jersey retired by Pleasant Grove High School, becoming the first player in school history to receive the honor.{{cite web|first=Brandon|last=Gurney|url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865647649/High-School-basketball-CJ-Wilcox-has-his-number-retired-at-Pleasant-Grove.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160214142329/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865647649/High-School-basketball-CJ-Wilcox-has-his-number-retired-at-Pleasant-Grove.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 14, 2016|title=High School basketball: CJ Wilcox has his number retired at Pleasant Grove|work=DeseretNews.com|date=February 12, 2016|accessdate=March 6, 2016}} ==College career== In November 2009, the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]] announced that Wilcox would redshirt the 2009–10 season.{{cite web|url=http://seattletimes.com/html/huskies/2010245512_umen11.html|title=Huskies will redshirt freshman guard C.J. Wilcox|work=SeattleTimes.com|date=November 10, 2009|accessdate=July 10, 2014}} In his freshman season at Washington in 2010–11, Wilcox was named to the Pac-10 All-Freshman team. In 33 games, he averaged 8.1 points and 2.1 rebounds in 15.8 minutes per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/cj-wilcox-1.html|title=C.J. Wilcox Stats|work=Sports-Reference.com|accessdate=July 10, 2014}} In his sophomore season, Wilcox was an Honorable Mention All-Pac-12 selection after his 73 three-pointers ranked 5th most in UW single-season history and moved to fifth all-time in UW history with 136 three-pointers. In 32 games, he averaged 14.2 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 28.5 minutes per game. In June 2012, he attended Kevin Durant's Skills Academy.{{cite web|url=http://www.nikeeyb.com/page/show/1182188-2012-roster|title=JUNE 27-29: KEVIN DURANT|work=nikeeyb.com|accessdate=July 10, 2014|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140702122644/http://www.nikeeyb.com/page/show/1182188-2012-roster|archivedate=July 2, 2014}} In his junior season, Wilcox earned second-team All-Pac-12 honors after scoring 570 points in 2012–13, the 11th highest UW single-season total. In 34 games, he averaged 16.8 points, 4.3 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.1 steals and 1.1 blocks in 34.8 minutes per game. In his senior season, Wilcox earned second-team All-Pac-12 honors for the second straight year after scoring 587 points in 2013–14, tying for the eighth highest UW single-season total. He was also named first-team all-district by the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] (NABC) and the [[United States Basketball Writers Association]] (USBWA).{{cite press release|title=2013-14 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Honors|date=March 10, 2014|access-date=March 10, 2014|publisher=Pac-12 Conference|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2014/3/10/2013-14-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140312033514/http://pac-12.com/article/2014/03/10/2013-14-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors|archive-date=March 12, 2014|url-status=live}}{{cite news|first=Percy|last=Allen|title=C.J. Wilcox earns postseason honors|date=March 13, 2014|accessdate=March 13, 2014|newspaper=The Seattle Times|url=http://blogs.seattletimes.com/huskymensbasketball/2014/03/13/c-j-wilcox-earns-postseason-honors/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140320040230/http://blogs.seattletimes.com/huskymensbasketball/2014/03/13/c-j-wilcox-earns-postseason-honors/|archivedate=March 20, 2014|url-status=live}} In 32 games, he averaged 18.3 points, 3.7 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.0 blocks in 34.9 minutes per game. Wilcox finished his career with 1,880 career points, which ranks second all-time at UW. He also finished with 98 blocked shots, which ranks fifth all-time and ranks top all-time amongst guards at UW.{{cite web|url=https://admin.xosn.com/pdf9/2910607.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=30200&|title=2014-15 Husky Basketball Record Book|page=39|format=PDF|accessdate=November 11, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150326182115/https://admin.xosn.com/pdf9/2910607.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=30200&|archive-date=March 26, 2015|url-status=dead}} He is also the Washington record holder for most career three-pointers made with 301, which also ranks sixth in Pac-12 history; is one of three players in Pac-12 history to record 1,700 career points, 275 career three-pointers and 400 career rebounds ([[Jason Kapono]], UCLA, 1999–03; [[Jason Gardner]], Arizona, 1999–03); and set Washington's single-season made three-point field goals record with 90 in 2013–14. ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Clippers (2014–2016)=== In May 2014, Wilcox was invited to the 2014 [[NBA Draft Combine]]{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Norlander|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24559610/official-2014-nba-pre-draft-combine-invite-list|title=Official 2014 NBA pre-draft combine invite list|work=CBSSports.com|date=May 12, 2014|accessdate=July 10, 2014}} where he performed well in athletic tests and was ranked one of the top shooters.{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Helfgot|url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865603334/Pleasant-Grove-native-CJ-Wilcox-impressing-NBA-teams-at-Chicago-combine.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140520233559/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865603334/Pleasant-Grove-native-CJ-Wilcox-impressing-NBA-teams-at-Chicago-combine.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 20, 2014|title=Pleasant Grove native C.J. Wilcox impressing NBA teams at Chicago combine|work=DeseretNews.com|date=May 16, 2014|accessdate=May 26, 2014}} On June 26, 2014, Wilcox was selected with the 28th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-select-wilcox|title=CLIPPERS SELECT C.J. WILCOX IN 2014 NBA DRAFT|work=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2014|accessdate=July 10, 2014}} On July 7, it was announced that Wilcox would miss the [[2014 NBA Summer League]] due to a right shoulder injury.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/bullock-wilcox-injury-release-update|title=CLIPPERS INJURY UPDATE|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2014|accessdate=July 10, 2014}} On July 12, he signed with the Clippers.{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=16221|title=Clippers sign first round draft pick C.J. Wilcox|work=InsideHoops.com|date=July 12, 2014|accessdate=July 12, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714191403/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=16221|archive-date=July 14, 2014|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/07/13/clippers-cj-wilcox.ap/index.html|title=Clippers sign draft pick C.J. Wilcox|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2014|accessdate=July 13, 2014}} Having appeared in just three games for the Clippers, he was assigned to the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA Development League]] on January 6, 2015.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/wilcox-assigned-d-league|title=Wilcox Assigned To D-League|work=NBA.com|date=January 6, 2015|accessdate=January 6, 2015}} On January 21, he was recalled by the Clippers.{{cite web|url=http://fortwayne.dleague.nba.com/news/cj-wilcox-recalled/|title=CJ Wilcox Recalled|work=NBA.com|date=January 21, 2015|accessdate=January 21, 2015}} On February 8, he scored a season-high 10 points in a loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/wilcocj01/gamelog/2015/|title=C.J. Wilcox 2014-15 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|accessdate=November 5, 2015}} In July 2015, Wilcox joined the Clippers for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]] where he averaged 14.0 points and 3.2 rebounds in five games. During the 2015–16 season, using the flexible assignment rule, Wilcox had multiple assignments to the [[Canton Charge]] and [[Northern Arizona Suns|Bakersfield Jam]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |title=2015-16 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|accessdate=March 6, 2016|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150628235947/http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/|archivedate=June 28, 2015}} ===Orlando Magic / Erie BayHawks (2016–2017)=== On July 15, 2016, Wilcox was traded, along with cash considerations, to the [[Orlando Magic]] in exchange for [[Devyn Marble]] and a future second round draft pick.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-acquire-cj-wilcox-clippers-20160715|title=Magic Acquire C.J. Wilcox From Clippers|work=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2016|accessdate=July 15, 2016}} On April 3, 2017, he was waived by the Magic. Wilcox played in 22 games with Orlando during the 2016–17 season. He also appeared in four games with the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA Development League]] on assignment, averaging 12.5 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.25 steals in 25.3 minutes per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-marcus-georges-hunt-and-patricio-garino|title=Magic Sign Marcus Georges-Hunt and Patricio Garino|work=NBA.com|date=April 3, 2017|accessdate=April 3, 2017}} ===Portland Trail Blazers / Santa Cruz Warriors (2017–2018)=== On August 9, 2017, Wilcox signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-guard-cj-wilcox-two-way-contract|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN GUARD CJ WILCOX TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|work=NBA.com|date=August 9, 2017|accessdate=August 9, 2017}} On October 23, he was ruled out for six to eight weeks after undergoing successful arthroscopy on his right knee.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/cj-wilcox-undergoes-successful-knee-arthroscopy|title=CJ WILCOX UNDERGOES SUCCESSFUL KNEE ARTHROSCOPY|work=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2017|accessdate=October 24, 2017}} He ultimately did not appear in a game for the Trail Blazers. === Indiana Pacers / Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2019–2020)=== Wilcox signed a two-way deal with the [[Indiana Pacers]] in August 2018. On September 21, 2018, it was announced that he had suffered a [[Achilles tendon rupture|torn Achilles tendon]] and would miss the entire season. On October 19, Wilcox was waived by the Pacers. {{cite news |title=Pacers' C.J. Wilcox: Tears Achilles, to miss 2018-19 season |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-c-j-wilcox-tears-achilles-to-miss-2018-19-season/ |accessdate=September 21, 2018 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=September 21, 2018}} On July 1, 2019, the [[Indiana Pacers]] re–signed Wilcox to an [[Exhibit 10]] contract.{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers Sign Bowen, Gant and Wilcox|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/indiana-pacers-sign-bowen-gant-and-wilcox|date=July 1, 2019|website=NBA.com|accessdate=July 1, 2019}} On October 16, 2019, Wilcox was waived by the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|title=Pacers Waive Three|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-three|date=October 16, 2019|website=NBA.com|accessdate=October 16, 2019}} On October 26, Wilcox was included in the training camp roster for the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=Stevens|url=https://fortwayne.gleague.nba.com/news/mad-ants-draft-two-players-announce-2019-training-camp-roster|title=Mad Ants draft two players, announce 2019 training camp roster|date=October 26, 2019|website=NBA.com|accessdate=October 26, 2019}} On November 6, Wilcox was included in the opening night roster of the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=Stevens|url=https://fortwayne.gleague.nba.com/news/mad-ants-finalize-2019-20-opening-night-roster|title=Mad Ants Finalize 2019-20 Opening Night Roster|date=November 6, 2019|website=NBA.com|accessdate=November 6, 2019}} On January 28, 2020, he posted 25 points, four rebounds, and two steals in a loss to the [[Salt Lake City Stars]].{{cite news |title=C.J. Wilcox: Paces team in scoring |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/c-j-wilcox-paces-team-in-scoring/ |accessdate=July 16, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 29, 2020}} Wilcox averaged 13.6 points and 2.7 rebounds per game.{{cite news |title=C.J. Wilcox: Productive scoring game Tuesday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/c-j-wilcox-productive-scoring-game-tuesday/ |accessdate=July 16, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 26, 2020}} On January 17, 2022, Wilcox's rights were traded from the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] to the [[Grand Rapids Gold]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=January 17, 2022|access-date=January 17, 2022}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- |style="text-align:left;"|[[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2010–11]] |style="text-align:left;"|[[2010–11 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]] |33||6||15.8||.419||.401||.806||2.1||.9||.4||.3||8.1 |- |style="text-align:left;"|[[2011–12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2011–12]] |style="text-align:left;"|[[2011–12 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]] |32||12||28.5||.437||.403||.839||3.4||1.2||.9||.6||14.2 |- |style="text-align:left;"|[[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13]] |style="text-align:left;"|[[2012–13 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]] |34||34||34.8||.419||.366||.816||4.3||1.9||1.1||1.1||16.8 |- |style="text-align:left;"|[[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–14]] |style="text-align:left;"|[[2013–14 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]] |32||32||34.9||.453||.391||.873||3.7||2.5||1.0||1.0||18.3 |} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2014}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2014–15 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A.
